//: Layer-2 constraint templates, keyed by the song/band symbol the adapter routes to (a set here OVERRIDES the same-named grammar symbol; the grammar stays a per-attempt fallback). Slot filters query the ontology-tagged pools in lexicon.ontology.json; mood constraints keep multi-slot titles coherent per the genre's mood threshold. Each set ends with a simple always-satisfiable template so generation never fails.
=== songTitle.traditionalPop (naming-genre-templates directive): the genre previously had NO song-title set at all and silently fell back to songTitle.jazz via the AdultPop family alias. ===

=== bandName.teenPop (naming-genre-templates directive): kept deliberately small and conservative — teen pop was overwhelmingly solo singers; most vocal groups belong in doo-wop/girl-group, later ones in bubblegum. ===
//album: Album slots use broad, evocative DOMAIN/MOOD filters (not the whole pool) so style-only words (Blessing/Creaking/Copper) don't leak in; the per-genre AFFINITY then flavors the choice within.
//: === Two-person billing. Routed for any act whose lineup is two people (ActNaming.ChooseBandSymbol). Person slots bind to the real members; the cast gate keeps kin billing to sibling acts. ===

=== NAMING v2 song-title sets (docs A/F): split the overloaded early60s/jazz/hardRock buckets + add the sets that were hitting grammar fallback (british/garage/protoPunk/funk). Routed via the TemplateRouter ancestry walk. ===

=== NAMING v2 solo-act sets (doc B): keyed soloAct.<genre>.<strategy>. The adapter picks a strategy (weighted per genre) then routes here via the ancestry walk. firstName filter "$name" and lastName "$surname" bind to the person the adapter rolled (gender+ethnicity); honorific "<tag> & $gender" auto-agrees with that gender (replaces doc B's genderAgree constraint). "groom" reshapes the first name (Robert->Bobby / Bob->Robert). ===

=== NAMING v2 album-title sets (doc C): per-genre LP architectures. %selfTitle% binds the act's own name and %leadSingle% the album's designated hit (adapter-injected via ctx.Slots); templates needing an absent lead single are dropped so each set still ends satisfiable. The frame carries genre identity more than the vocabulary does. ===
